newsitem.title: CANADA: Bank of Canada saw low inflation, strong demand.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Canada saw low inflation, strong demand.

text.p: The Bank of Canada's board of directors foresaw lower inflation, strong domestic demand and economic growth ahead for Canada, extracts of the board's meeting on February 13 show.

"The Governor (Gordon Thiessen) said that, with business confidence remaining high and consumer confidence improving, domestic demand could be expected to remain strong in the first quarter of 1997," the minutes, released on Wednesday, said.
But the bank said Canada still has "significant" slack in its product and labor markets.
Because of the slack, the bank said it expected inflation to trend downward, sticking to the lower part of the bank's one-to-three percent target range in the coming months.
According to the minutes, Thiessen also said that international economic conditions should continue to help the Canadian economy expand in the period ahead.
He pointed to firm commodities prices as well as momentum in the U.S. economy, which he expected to offset a weaker outlok for Europe and Japan.
He said that while interest rates have remained steady since October 1996, the end of the year was dominated by swings in the value of the Canadian dollar.
"The Governor noted that the Canadian dollar had fluctuated considerably since early December but that, on balance, it had not changed much," the minutes reported.
The board also said that the rapid growth in Canada's money supply in 1996 was "consistent with continued low inflation and a strengthening of economic activity."
